title: Drishyam 3 Records 24.58 Lakh Day-One Footfalls, Bollywood's 10th-Highest Post-COVID
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's franchise finale collected 62 crore net on day one, finishing just below Tiger 3 in tickets sold while out-earning it in rupee terms.
body:
• Drishyam 3 sold an estimated 24.58 lakh tickets on its opening day, registering Bollywood's 10th-highest day-one footfalls in the post-COVID era — the only crime thriller on the list.
  • The Ajay Devgn starrer collected 62 crore net in India on day one across 15,759 shows, with Sacnilk reporting 2,458,370 tickets sold.
  • It finished just below Salman Khan's Tiger 3 (24.91 lakh) in footfalls, even as it out-collected Pathaan, Gadar 2, War 2 and Tiger in rupee terms — a gap explained by higher ticket rates.
  • Day two is projected at 40–45 crore net, which would take the film past the 100-crore mark in India within its opening weekend.

Drishyam 3 has converted franchise goodwill into hard numbers. The concluding chapter of the Vijay Salgaonkar saga sold an estimated 24.58 lakh tickets on its first day in India, entering Bollywood's top 10 day-one footfalls in the post-COVID era — a list on which it is the only crime thriller.

As per the official update, the Abhishek Pathak-directed film amassed 62 crore net at the Indian box office on day one, driven by strong walk-in audiences on top of advance bookings. Sacnilk's figures match: 2,458,370 footfalls across 15,759 shows.

"Thriller genre re-defined. And this is coming without any premieres or paid previews."

— Nishit Shaw, box office observer, as quoted by Filmibeat

Context & Background

The opening-day momentum built through the day. By 1 pm on Friday, October 2, the film had earned 18.51 crore from morning shows alone — already ahead of Drishyam 2's full opening-day collection of 15.38 crore. Morning occupancy stood at 46.3 percent across India, beating Ranveer Singh's Dhurandhar 2 (43.15 percent), and BookMyShow recorded roughly 300,000 ticket sales between 6 am and 1 pm — about 11 tickets every second.

The Gandhi Jayanti national holiday amplified turnout. With 62 crore net in India, 74.4 crore India gross, 18.5 crore overseas and 92.9 crore worldwide on day one, the film also recorded Bollywood's second-highest worldwide opening of 2026.

Impact & Analysis

The footfalls ranking tells a subtler story than the collections chart. Drishyam 3 sits 10th, just below Tiger 3's 24.91 lakh, while ranking ahead of Pathaan (57 crore), Gadar 2 (40.1 crore), War 2 (52.5 crore) and Tiger (44.5 crore) in rupee collections but below them in tickets sold — the mark of premium ticket pricing converting fewer seats into bigger revenue.

The full post-COVID top 10 reads: Adipurush (55.83 lakh), Jawan (44.36 lakh), Animal (39.7 lakh), Dhurandhar 2 (38.9 lakh), Pathaan (31.06 lakh), Stree 2 (27.9 lakh), Gadar 2 (26.78 lakh), War 2 (24.97 lakh), Tiger 3 (24.91 lakh) and Drishyam 3 (24.58 lakh). That a mid-budget crime thriller — a genre driven by word of mouth rather than spectacle — cracked a list dominated by action epics is the more remarkable achievement.

The Drishyam franchise's arc explains the urgency. Since the makers confirmed this is the conclusion, curiosity about Vijay Salgaonkar's final chapter created genuine first-day urgency among moviegoers, with strong word of mouth spreading through the day.

Diaspora Angle

The Drishyam brand travels well beyond India — the Malayalam originals spawned remakes in multiple languages and a devoted following among diaspora audiences in the Gulf, North America and the UK, where day-one shows for the finale also reported strong turnout.

What's Next

After a 62-crore start, day two is projected at 40–45 crore net, which would push the film past 100 crore net in India within its opening weekend and set up a race toward the 200-crore lifetime mark. The real test begins Monday, when the holiday effect wears off.
